Advertisements will land in Apple Maps in the US and Canada this summer. Ahead of the launch, Apple is sharing more details about what Apple Maps ads will and won't allow.

Apple Maps ads are coming, and Apple is revealing the banned categories

Apple first announced its plans to bring ads to Apple Maps back in March. The company said ads would appear at the top of search results, as well as in a new widget in the app called "Suggested Places."

Apple laid the groundwork back in May with iOS 26.5, which included the new Suggested Places feature. However, the company hasn't shared any further details about the actual launch of Apple Maps ads since then.

According to TechCrunch, Apple has now updated its Apple Advertising Services policy with new information about Apple Maps.

That policy covers the general ad details for services including Apple News, Stocks, and Maps, and lists a long list of banned ad content covering things like violence, weapons, drugs, and more that apply across all services.

However, the most interesting details reveal more about what Apple Maps ads won't allow. Apple says Apple Maps ads have three additional banned categories:

  • Home services: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes home services, including but not limited to plumbing, locksmiths, HVAC, pest control, roofing, or general contracting services.
  • Bail bonds: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes bail bond or surety bond services in connection with criminal pretrial detention.
  • Crypto ATMs: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes cryptocurrency ATMs.

Additionally, Apple says ads related to medical services will be evaluated on a "case-by-case" basis.

As TechCrunch points out, Apple's blanket ban on "home services" advertising is interesting. Home services are one of the main ad categories on Google Maps, but Apple seemingly has zero interest in bringing them to Apple Maps.

All signs point to Apple being on the verge of launching ads in Apple Maps. However, there's still no formal launch date as of yet.

Check out the full list of banned ad categories for all Apple services on the company's website.
